episodes.190829: An approaching upper level low over northern AZ and the Four Corners region overrode abundant low level moisture moving northward into eastern NM. Discrete severe storms developed over portions of northeastern NM during the afternoon with a second area of strong to severe storms located close to the center of the upper level low in northwestern NM. Severe wind gusts and small hail was reported from the discrete storm cells across northeastern NM. These storm cells coalesced and migrated southeastward into the east-central plains of Quay, Curry and Roosevelt Counties by the evening where they produced heavy rainfall that resulted in flash Flooding in Clovis, NM. Earlier, strong wind gusts, accumulating small hail and a landspout were reported with the convection over extremely remote areas of northwestern NM. These storm cells eventually progressed into the Rio Grande Valley where severe winds reached the Albuquerque metro. ||Key Words: Hail, Thunderstorm Wind Gust, Landspout, Flash Flooding.

episodes.190957: Severe thunderstorms developed in the afternoon of June 13th ahead of an approaching cold front. Supercells initially produced large hail in northeast Missouri before transitioning into mostly a wind threat as they neared the Mississippi River. Further south, semi-discrete convection produced damaging winds in Boone County later that evening.

A strong/severe storm formed over southwest Denver where hail just reached one inch in diameter. Storms increased in coverage and intensity as they tracked into Washington County.

episodes.191201: Low pressure off the southern California coast pulled mid level moisture from Mexico into the Colorado River Valley. This moisture plus hot surface air fueled isolated thunderstorms, and the hot, dry low level air led to a microburst.
episodes.191239: An area of low pressure moved across southern Ontario/Quebec with it's associated cold front sweeping across northern NY during the late night hours of June 13th to just past midnight on June 14th. episodes.191874: Multiple rounds of training thunderstorms produced an extended period of torrential rainfall across Cheyenne and Morrill counties from the mid to late afternoon into the early evening hours on 6/14. Numerous reports were received of rainfall amounts ranging from 3 to 5 inches in a short period of time, resulting in flash flooding of several county roads due to creeks and streams flowing out of their banks and ditches quickly filling up.
episodes.191930: A few isolated thunderstorms produced quarter size hail and wind gusts around 60 mph.
episodes.192225: Thunderstorms developed along a stalled out frontal boundary, which was situated across the middle of Nebraska. As these storms tracked to the southeast, they became severe over southwestern Nebraska. Thunderstorm wind gusts up to 60 MPH were reported along with flash flooding between Lisco and Oshkosh.
episodes.192296: A cold front triggered clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms across north-central Illinois during the evening of June 13th into the pre-dawn hours of June 14th.  Most of the activity was focused along and north of a Beardstown to Champaign line.  Numerous trees and power lines were blown down thanks to 60-70 mph wind gusts, while a few reports of hail as large as quarters were also received.  The most significant wind damage occurred across northeastern McLean County from Chenoa and Lexington southeastward through Cropsey and Anchor where a damage survey team determined widespread wind gusts of 80-110 mph as well as 5 tornado touchdowns.  A total of 33 high-tension electrical transmission towers were severely damaged as a result of the powerful winds across this area.
episodes.192305: A cold front moved through the Ohio Valley, producing scattered showers and thunderstorms.
episodes.192346: One lone thunderstorm on the morning of the 13th produced severe winds over portions of the Chicago metro. Additional clusters of strong to severe storms developed that  afternoon and evening mainly impacting areas south of I-80 with severe winds and one tornado.
episodes.192354: Strong thunderstorms moved over northwest Indiana on the evening of the 13th producing one report of severe winds in Lowell.
episodes.192520: The combined OK/TX Panhandles were hit with a gusty line of storms both on the 13th and 14th of June. Severe winds were the main story with these storms. Ground stations measured wind gusts as high as 80 mph with the storms on the 13th. Then on the 14th, multiple reports of wind damage were made with estimated winds as high as 85 mph, as multiple train cars were knocked over in Cimarron County in OK along with a gain silo damaged in Dallam County in TX.  Then on the 15th Beaver County did see a discrete storm produce some large hail.

episodes.192682: A cold front crossed the region during the afternoon of the 14th. Thunderstorms developed in advance of the cold front. An isolated storm reached severe levels across Penobscot county producing large hail.
episodes.192744: A warm, moist, and unstable air mass across the region ahead of a southward sinking cold front resulted in thunderstorm development, with several being severe. These produced large hail and scattered damaging winds. Most hail reports ranged in size from quarter to golf ball size hail. The largest hail fell in Van Buren County near Keosauqua where 2 to 3 inch diameter hail fell. There were also a few reports of 60 to 80 MPH across far southeast Iowa into west central Illinois, which damaged trees and knocked down several outbuildings.  The most widespread damage occurred near Oakville, IA.  Two brief, non-damaging tornadoes were also seen north of Macomb, IL.

episodes.192900: On the afternoon of June 14th, a few hours of strong to severe thunderstorms were observed within southeast Ohio. This was the result of a passing cold front tapping into warm surface temperatures, and firing up storms quickly after sunrise across the Ohio Valley. The bulk of the storm damage was observed in the form of downed trees and power lines within southeast Ohio, but an isolated observation of sub-severe hail in Morgan County also occurred. By the evening on the 14th, storms progressed east of the Ohio River into West Virginia, bringing the severe threat in Ohio to an end.
episodes.192952: A broken line of convection, ahead of a weak cold front, dropped south through north central Kentucky. The line that stretched from the Louisville area through the Bluegrass region produced one stronger storm that caused tree damage in Nelson County.
episodes.193175: Late evening thunderstorms caused by a pre-frontal trough tracked southeast out of Canada and across the north country on June 13th. A few of these storms were severe as they tracked into the forecast area.

episodes.193312: Scattered thunderstorms developed over Yuma County during the afternoon hours producing sub-severe wind gusts up to 55 mph and hail the size of dimes and quarters. The largest hail was reported north of the town of Eckley, Colorado.
episodes.193350: Several severe storms produce large hail up to softball size in the evening hours.
episodes.193559: High winds and damage occurred from thunderstorms overnight on the 13th into the morning of the 14th.
episodes.193672: High based thunderstorms developed in the Big Horn Basin and brought high wind gusts. The south Big Horn County airport had a wind gust to 71 mph. Near Worland, another microburst downed multiple trees.

episodes.193851: A trough of low pressure tracking east over California nudged the subtropical high eastward into the Southern Plains in the days leading up to this event. This allowed some monsoonal moisture to trickle into the Four Corners region. On the day of the event, the low crossed the Four Corners, adding some extra lift and instability. The most widespread coverage was south of the I-70 corridor, although that didn't stop a few showers and storms from firing off the higher terrain along and north of I-70. Dry surface levels kept the main threats to being gusty winds and maybe some small hail.

Whenever enough moisture and instability is present, a thunderstorm forms along the Utah Tavaputs near the McCook Ridge RAWS site. Multiple photos and a video were shared on Twitter/X showing a well defined landspout beneath a strong thunderstorm cell just northwest of Crownpoint, NM. The video clearly shows the landspout north to northeast of the intersection of Navajo Service Route 89 and Navajo Service Route 9. Subsequent photos and radar support the track of the landspout moving east toward NM Highway 371 north of Crownpoint. No damage was reported and is not surprising given the extremely remote location. Location and track are based on the combination of analysis of the photos, video and radar data.

An EF-0 strength landspout tornado occurred in Lawrence Township in Mercer County. The landspout began near the Marwa Service Center and Conoco gas station near the intersection of Johnson Road and US Route 1 Business (Brunswick Avenue), where a few trees were uprooted and some softwood trees were snapped. A couple trees|fell on the service station, causing some collateral damage. The gas station canopy was not damaged, but a large sign behind the building was snapped. Two large clothes donation bins were tossed into a brushy area. Surveillance footage from the service center showed a distinct convergent nature and shift to the winds as the damage occurred.||The landspout then moved northeast into a small wooded area before emerging into a post office parking lot. About a half dozen vehicles were flipped over in the parking lot, and a few parking lot signs were blown over or lofted and carried about 250 yards |away across the highway. The post office building sustained some minor structural damage, including uplift of some metal roofing material. An HVAC unit was blown off of the roof of the building. A large tree was uprooted at the front of the building and a few |other trees had several limbs blown down. Cell phone footage taken from across the highway at the Auto Lenders property showed a distinct circulation as the damage was occurring, lofting debris vertically. The landspout then dissipated after impacting the post office property and no additional damage was observed downstream.
